title: What drinking-water guideline values for metals were verified?

grade.title: Small, uncontrolled, or single-source human evidence
grade.outcome: WHO values for lead, cadmium, and nickel
grade.basis: Each value is recorded from one citing document. The WHO book itself was not the file checked for arsenic, chromium, or mercury.

answerHtml: The corpus records three WHO drinking-water values as checked through other agency documents: lead 10 µg/L provisional, cadmium 3 µg/L, and nickel 70 µg/L. Arsenic, chromium, and mercury values in the same guideline were not re-read and are not stated. These are guideline figures, not measurements of a tap.

sections.heading: Values used
sections.html:
Cobalt: the ATSDR 2024 profile, as recorded in the corpus, says WHO has no guideline value. WHO GDWQ.

Drinking-water figures published on this site

Cadmium 3 µg/L Corpus, via ATSDR cadmium draft (2026)
Nickel 70 µg/L Corpus, cited in EFSA 2020

heavyMetalIndexHtml: Heavy Metal Index: water. This Heavy Metal Index URL returned HTTP 200 on 15 October 2026. Figures on this page are not copied from that index. They come from the sources named above.
buyHtml:
The Heavy Metal Tested and Certified public register listed no licensees on 15 October 2026. That page reported 0 certified brands and 0 certified products, and it stated that no brand has completed the three-lot baseline. A specimen layout on the register is an illustration, not a licensee. This page does not name or rank any brand.

The program states that certification is a measurement of a product against a published limit, not a statement that the product is safe. If a licensee is later listed for this category, it will be on the register.

  • Heavy Metal Tested and Certified
  • Public register of licensees
footnote: This page summarizes cited documents. It does not diagnose or prescribe. Reviewed 15 October 2026.
